$comment: EXAMPLE of the per-designer mapping. The real file lives OUTSIDE the repo at ~/.figma-sync/mappings.json and is created/updated by the figma-sync commands. It records, per flow: the Figma file, the iOS and Android section nodes, and the iOS<->Android screen-node pairs. create-android/create-ios WRITE it; sync-screens READS it to detect drift and also WRITES it on an approved sync (re-baselining snapshots, setting lastSyncedAt/lastSyncDirection, and ADDING a screenPair for a built screen or DROPPING one for a removed screen); apply-ds-update READS it to build its per-platform work set and WRITES two per-flow fields on a successful apply: dsVersion (the registry `version` the flow's platform section was last brought to) and dsAppliedAt (ISO date of that apply). Together they let apply-ds-update skip flows already at the current registry version and resume a partial fan-out; a flow lacking them is treated as never-DS-updated. Each screenPair MAY also carry per-side content snapshots (iosSnapshot / androidSnapshot): the captured content of that screen at the last sync. A snapshot has a DUAL ROLE — it is both the drift baseline (diff live content against it to attribute who changed) and the rollback record (restore content from it). Snapshots hold CONTENT ONLY (text, image refs, structure hash, CTA label, screen fill) — never chrome (status bar, app bar, nav, gesture/home indicator) or font family, which differ by platform by design and are not drift. ALL snapshot/sync/ds fields are OPTIONAL and back-compatible: an entry written by an older create-* run (no snapshots, no lastSyncDirection, no dsVersion/dsAppliedAt) is still valid and simply degrades to live-only detection and never-DS-updated. Each flow also carries an optional flowId that cross-links this mapping to an in-file IDENTITY STAMP that create-android/create-ios/build-page write onto the section node via Figma setPluginData (figmaSyncFlowId, figmaSyncRole = ios|android, figmaSyncPairId linking the two counterpart sections). That stamp — NOT spatial position or section name — is the source of truth for a flow's identity and its iOS<->Android pairing; the commands' idempotency guard resolves an existing counterpart through it. build-page (multi-section pages, where one page holds many flows) READS the stamp to classify and reconcile a whole page, and WRITES/relocates entries — recording an adopted legacy section's inferred-then-confirmed pairing. flowId is OPTIONAL and back-compatible: an entry without it degrades to classifier-inferred identity. The stamp holds identity ONLY — never layout coordinates (build-page keeps its reversible layout backup in-canvas) or chrome/content.
